Each retry created a brand-new HTTP connection instead of reusing the pooled client, so most of the observed latency was TLS handshake overhead rather than the SMS provider itself.

question: In GoF Design Patterns Scalable Systems, how does invariant verification safeguard production performance under heavy load?

options.text: By establishing deterministic resource bounds and validated constraints for gof design patterns scalable systems.
By wrapping every method call in a Decorator purely for logging, on the assumption that decoration alone bounds retries or resource usage.
By routing every request through a long Chain of Responsibility so more handlers get a chance to validate it, regardless of whether each handler stays within its own resource bounds.
By using the Singleton pattern for shared state so there is only one copy in memory, without validating that concurrent access to it is otherwise safe.
